title: Levin's decapitated flatworms keep their memories
summary: Rupert Sheldrake tells of Levin's decapitated flatworms keep their memories, about an unknown time at Tufts University, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: he trained these flat worms to respond to particular stimuli that he could measure their response they learned the effect then he cut their heads off

related.note: This is the same flatworm memory experiment as #9, but it puts forward morphic resonance in place of the conventional explanation.

plain: A biologist known for unusual ideas, Rupert Sheldrake, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2024, describes experiments by Michael Levin, a biologist at Tufts University in Massachusetts. Sheldrake says Levin trained flatworms to respond to certain stimuli, then cut their heads off, and that the worms kept what they had learned after regrowing. If true, memory would not be stored only in the brain.
